rv.q: If the production doesn't, for imaginative coherence, achieve the standard set by Lloyd's Macbeth, I hope it won't be long before Freeman broaches the Bard for a second time.
Other warnings might have been issued. These would concern imposing a complicated back-story on an already knotted plot.
But Jamie Lloyd’s production isn’t terribly convincing on any level, and it suffers from an emphasis on concept over character.
This, however, is director’s theatre at its self-advertising worst, while Freeman gives a disappointingly underpowered performance as Richard, normally one of the most thrilling roles in Shakespeare.
Jamie Lloyd's vigorous production is remarkable for its fierce lucidity.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this stylized production, with Freeman's Richard deemed disappointingly tame and Lloyd's directorial choices polarizing. Some praise its Tarantino-esque violence, while others find it self-indulgent.
